newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Dostum army digs in against Taleban, no fighting.
newsitem.headline: Dostum army digs in against Taleban, no fighting.

text.p: Tanks, heavy artillery and muliple launch Grad missiles of warlord Abdul Rashid Dostum were dug in at both ends of the vital Salang tunnel northwest of the Afghan capital Kabul on Wednesday.

Colonel-General Chary, commander of Dostum's Jumbish-i-Milli frontline position told reporters there had been no fighting with the Islamic Taleban militia deployed nearby. He added: "We don't want to fight but we will defend our territory."
Reuters correspondent Chris Bird saw tanks, heavy artillery and Grad missile launchers placed at both ends of the strategically vital tunnel, around 70 km (45 miles) northwest of Kabul.
Chary, speaking at his position overlooking the village of Olang, said Taleban forces were around 3 km (2 miles) to the south. "We command the heights -- there has been no fighting here," he said.
Taleban Acting Deputy Foreign Minister Sher Mohammed Stanakzai told reporters on Tuesday their forces did not want to fight Dostum.
